summary: Crash after attempting to move item from off-hand in Creative inventory
description: A crash is caused when trying to offhand an item in the creative inventory after attempting to do so in the search tab Steps to reproduce: - Have an item in your off-hand in creative mode - Open inventory and go to the Search tab - Use the off-hand key to try and put the item in your off-hand into the hotbar (stopped as the search box takes priority) - Change back to the Survival Inventory tab, and then press the off-hand key again without hovering cursor over any inventory slots or: - Have an item in your off-hand in creative mode - Hover over any empty slot in a tab other than Survival Inventory - Select the Survival Inventory tab, and then press the off-hand key without hovering cursor over any inventory slots As far as I can tell (Not a programmer or anything, didn t look at code, just from my small testing) this happens because the offhand hotkey when pressed tries to put the item in your offhand into the last inventory slot that you had "selected" (hovered over) with your cursor. When you try to use the offhand hotkey when under the search tab, the search box takes priority and types instead of allowing you to offhand, making it the last selected inventory "slot" (I believe,) when you change back to your player inventory tab, there s no textbox anymore, so when you try to use the hotkey again, the game crashes as there s no "last selected" slot to offhand to (or maybe because it tries to offhand to the textbox? I dunno I m not a programmer) Simply hovering over an inventory slot after swapping to the player inventory before using the offhand hotkey will prevent the crash and allow the hotkey to work as normal.
Steps to Reproduce:
1. Launch Minecraft in Creative mode.
2. Ensure you have an item in your off-hand.
3. Open your inventory and navigate to the Search tab.
4. Attempt to use the off-hand key to move the item from your off-hand into the hotbar.
5. Change back to the Survival Inventory tab.
6. Press the off-hand key again without hovering your cursor over any inventory slots.
7. Observe that the game crashes.
8. Alternatively, hover over any empty slot in a tab other than Survival Inventory.
9. Select the Survival Inventory tab.
10. Press the off-hand key without hovering your cursor over any inventory slots.
11. Observe that the game crashes again.
Observed Behavior: The actual behavior of the bug involves a crash occurring when a player attempts to use the off-hand key to transfer an item from the off-hand to the hotbar while in the Creative inventory, specifically after previously interacting with the search tab. The sequence begins with the player holding an item in the off-hand while in Creative mode. Upon opening the inventory and navigating to the Search tab, pressing the off-hand key does not successfully move the item because the search box takes precedence, resulting in text input rather than item transfer. When the player switches back to the Survival Inventory tab and presses the off-hand key again without having the cursor over any inventory slots, the game crashes. Alternatively, the crash can also occur if the player hovers over an empty slot in any tab other than the Survival Inventory, selects the Survival Inventory tab, and then presses the off-hand key without hovering over any slots. This issue seems to stem from the off-hand hotkey trying to place the item into the last selected inventory slot, which becomes problematic after using the search tab, as there is no valid slot available for the item to be transferred to when the player attempts to use the hotkey again. If the player hovers over an inventory slot after returning to the player inventory before using the off-hand key, the crash is avoided, and the hotkey functions normally.
Expected Behavior: When attempting to move an item from the off-hand to the hotbar while in the Creative inventory, the game should allow the action to complete without crashing. The off-hand key should successfully place the item into the selected hotbar slot, regardless of whether the player previously interacted with the search tab. The game should maintain a valid last selected inventory slot, ensuring that pressing the off-hand key functions correctly without causing a crash.
